summary:
**Conversation Overview**

This was Chat 10 of an ongoing long-form technical project called "The Method 1.6," in which Matthew is constructing a physics book with an accompanying structured register of approximately 1,557 entries. The session opened with Claude reading HANDOFF-11 and following its BRIDGE protocol: splitting two BUILD-10 bundles into the container's working directory, recovering 50 files, and verifying the Register's entry count and main volume's numeric count lines against the handoff's stated values. No volumes changed this chat; all BUILD-9 and BUILD-10 presses from prior sessions remained current.

The primary work of the chat was locating, fetching, and verifying a new data archive called `spectra_selection_and_levels.zip` (Drive id `1uo4n2GGrdCqP9VddW5nOGzaTJBoqkb-N`, sha256 prefix `866b0368`) relevant to two open items: 126 unreconciled Spectra rows and 45 Spectra rows previously marked no-data. Early fetch attempts failed because the Drive connector returns zip content as base64 in context only, never touching disk, and Claude's initial attempts to transcribe ~100 KB of base64 in single steps crashed multiple turns. Matthew resolved the size barrier by unzipping the archive directly in Drive. Once the 15 extracted files became visible to the connector, Claude fetched each file individually, wrote it to `/home/claude/req2/` via base64 heredoc, decoded it, and verified sha256 first-16 characters against the MANIFEST — all 10 fetched files matched exactly. The MANIFEST also records two formal corrections: (B) the six no-data species (Bi III, C I, Cd II, Hg II, N I, Sc III) were present in the bank all along, refuting the prior stated reason for the 45 no-data rows; and (A) the generator's bank register tops at R 1700. T8-CENSUS was read in full: of 554 rows, limits agree 391/554; 222 stored fallbacks reproduce at 221/222; 145 voided rows reproduce perfectly. One gap was identified: `store_gen.py` is absent from the MANIFEST and Drive, blocking blind re-run of the generator, but not blocking record-vs-record reconciliation.

Claude built HANDOFF-12 capturing the full session state, all 15 Drive file IDs, all 14 MANIFEST hashes, the proven fetch pipeline, T8-CENSUS findings, the store_gen.py gap, and a four-step chat-11 plan (split BUILD-10, fetch and verify MEASUREMENTS-DERIVED and STORE-RECONSTRUCT by ID, reconcile against the Spectra table and run489 `unrec`, register entries for corrections A and B). Matthew was advised to add HANDOFF-12 to project knowledge and retire nothing, with optional Drive housekeeping to remove duplicate extracted files. The session closed with Matthew confirming and Claude providing the opening prompt for chat 11.

**Tool Knowledge**

Google Drive `download_file_content` returns file content as base64 encoded text within Claude's context window only — nothing is written to the container's filesystem automatically. For small text files this is workable: write the base64 string to a `.b64` temp file via heredoc, run `base64 -d .b64 > outputfile`, then `sha256sum outputfile | cut -c1-16` and compare against the MANIFEST's recorded hash. This pipeline proved reliable for files up to ~7.8 KB (series_gen.py) with zero corruption across all 10 verified files. For larger files (MEASUREMENTS-DERIVED at 90 KB, STORE-RECONSTRUCT at 126 KB, READING-LIST-STAGING at 243 KB) this same approach applies but must be chunked across multiple turns to avoid context crashes — each chunk written and appended before decoding. Direct chat upload is preferable for archives above ~77 KB but may be blocked by the client. Drive search using `title contains 'filename'` failed to find freshly extracted files for several minutes after extraction; using exact `title = 'filename'` syntax also failed initially. Files became visible only after a delay or after Matthew confirmed their names explicitly, at which point `title = 'exact_name'` searches succeeded. Duplicate files from repeated extraction runs appear in search results with identical sizes; the newest copy by modification date should be

| \*\*g ≤ q\*\* | conservation of the placed |  
| \*\*2S ≤ k\*\* | the multiplicity a subshell can carry |  
| \*\*k ≥ 1\*\* | \*definitional\* — a transition needs a mover |

The whole of this work is one recursion, stated at §14.5.2:

| ratio | \*\*14.6 : 1\*\* |

\# THE METHOD 1.6 — THE INDEX OF INDICES  
  
Generated on 2026-08-15 by \`indices.py\`. \*\*Every index this work builds  
on or beside the atomic index — what it holds, whether it closes, whether it carries time, and  
what role it plays for Λ.\*\* Measured where measurable; where an index is named and never built,  
that is stated rather than filled in.  
  
\---  
  
\# I · THE ATOMIC INDEX ITSELF  
  
\*\*Λ = { (n, ℓ, k, q, e, f, g, 2S) ∈ ℤ⁸ : eight constraints, at caps }.\*\*  
  
\!\[\*\*Figure 1.\*\* Λ₈'s constraint graph. Seven bounds on eight coordinates — a caterpillar with 2S pendant at k. Every edge is a single monotone inequality except one: \*\*g takes two parents\*\*, and g ≤ min(q, 4f+2) is the only non-product term in the whole expression.\](figures-compendia/fig-i3-lambda8.png)  
  
A cell is a \*\*transition\*\*: a source subshell (n, ℓ) holding k electrons, q of them moving, into a  
target subshell (e, f) that ends with g, at spin 2S. \*\*Not a state — a move.\*\* Everything else in  
this document follows from that.  
  
| constraint | reads |  
|---|---|  
| \*\*ℓ ≤ n − 1\*\* | hydrogenic — the subshell fits its shell |  
| \*\*k ≤ 4ℓ + 2\*\* | \*\*Pauli\*\* — the subshell's capacity |  
| \*\*q ≤ k\*\* | conservation of the removed — you cannot take more than is held |  
| \*\*f ≤ e − 1\*\* | hydrogenic again, on the target |

and it is the Pauli principle. Remove it and 976 becomes 1,000; the 24 excluded cells all have  
f = 0 and g = 3 — three electrons in an s orbital.

\# THE METHOD 1.6 — SPECTRA COMPENDIUM  
  
\*\*The index of Rydberg channels, and a value for every cell of it.\*\*  
  
This compendium supplies the book with coordinates. Its subject is Λ\_spectra; its output is a defect for every channel of every element, graded by how the value was got. \*The register carries the working record — the corrections, the reversals, and what remains open. This carries the answers.\*  
  
\---  
  
\# 0 · THE COORDINATE SUPPLY  
  
\#\#\# What a coordinate is  
  
 (Z, charge, ℓ, 2S+1) → δ, with a grade, a source and a bound  
  
\*\*Z\*\* the atomic number · \*\*charge\*\* the ionisation stage, 1 for the neutral · \*\*ℓ\*\* the Rydberg orbital · \*\*2S+1\*\* the multiplicity, which Hund's rule on the core derives from the ground state and does not require measuring.  
  
\*\*δ\*\* is the quantum defect: E = −Z\_c²R/(n−δ)², so a channel's whole Rydberg series follows from one number and the core charge.  
  
\*\*DECLARATION — the stored δ is the MEDIAN over a cell's members (T2, closed).\*\* This was measured, not chosen: of 433 series whose member count reproduces exactly from raw, the stored value equals the median in 430 (99.3%); the 18 mean-agreements are series where median and mean coincide and distinguish nothing (R 1673, 1675, enlarged sample R 1679). The mean and asymptotic perspectives are carried alongside per cell, as perspectives of one definition (T6, M's ruling, session 1.7.3).

| \*\*computed\*\* | \*\*103,545\*\* | supplied by the channel equation, within the domain stated below |

\# The Physics Compendium  
  
Generated from \`mathreg.py\` and \`SPECTRA-DATA.tsv\` on 2026-08-12. \*\*248 registered objects, 17 of them physical mechanisms.\*\*  
  
This compendium states the \*\*interface\*\* between a physical quantity and the index that holds it. It is not a list of mechanisms — those are in \`MECHANISMS.md\` and the Mathematical Compendium, and a third copy would drift as register 778's list did. It states, for each index, what the cells stand for, what number is attached to them, the rule taking one to the other, which constants that rule requires, \*\*what must be measured rather than computed\*\*, and what physics does and does not do.  
  
Four faults in a single session were transitions performed without their rule written down: register 868 used R∞ for every species where the reduced-mass constant is correct; register 879 wrote Li III's ionisation limit as a formula where a measurement was required; register 766 passed atomic numbers where the core's charge is needed; register 782 set a verification column equal to its own denominator. \*\*This document exists because those four share one cause.\*\*  
  
\---  
  
\#\# Λ — the elemental index  
  
\*\*What it indexes.\*\* Electron configurations of the ground states of the elements, on eight coordinates (n, ℓ, k, q, e, f, g, 2S). \*\*976 cells.\*\*  
  
\*\*The quantity.\*\* None. A cell of Λ carries no physical number: it is an \*arrangement\*, not a measurement.  
  
\*\*The transition.\*\* A configuration is read off the aufbau order and its subshells mapped to coordinates. \`L.real\` establishes that Λ's eight constraints hold on 247 real subshells across all 118 elements — \*\*18,288 tests, no failures\*\*.  
  
\*\*Constants required.\*\* None.  
  
\*\*Must be measured.\*\* Nothing. Λ is closed — |Λ| = |ℛ(Λ)| = 976, \*\*E(Λ) = 0\*\* — and the partition identity holds exactly: 6,912 = 976 + 0 + 5,936 (register 833).  
  
\*\*What physics does.\*\* It supplies the aufbau ordering and the shell capacities, and nothing else. \*\*What it does NOT do:\*\* confer predictive power. §24 states that Λ \*"contains no physics that was not already in the quantum numbers; it is a recoding … a recoding adds nothing."\* Register 834 measured the consequence: on the same closed index, the T-bracket passes 789 of 789 and the δ-bracket passes 546 of 789. \*\*Closure coexists with a bracket that holds and one that fails, so it cannot be what makes either true.\*\*  
  
\---  
  
\#\# Λ\_spectra — the index of Rydberg channels  
  
\*\*What it indexes.\*\* Rydberg series: a fixed parent core, a fixed ℓ, n running. \*\*596 channels across 70 spectra, 2,269 interior cells.\*\* The complete index over the same alphabets is closed: |X| = |ℛ(X)| = 624, \*\*E = 0\*\* (register 853).  
  
\*\*The quantity.\*\* The \*\*quantum defect\*\* δ — a continuous real number measuring how far the Rydberg orbital penetrates the ionic core. It is not an integer and has no factorization (register 896).  
  
\*\*The transition.\*\* For a level at energy E below a limit I,  
  
 n\* = Z\_c √( R\_M / (I − E) ) δ = n − n\*  
  
\*\*Constants required, and which value:\*\*  
  
 - \*\*Z\_c — the charge of the CORE, not the atom.\*\* NIST states the formula as E\_nl = −Z\_c²/(n−δ)², \*"where Z\_c is the charge of the core"\*. Be III and B III are third spectra and take Z\_c = 3, not 4 and 5. Passing atomic numbers gave defects of −2 to −5 with spreads above 1.0 (registers 766, 883).  
 - \*\*R\_M — the reduced-mass Rydberg, R∞/(1 + mₑ/M), not R∞.\*\* For helium 109,722.386 against 109,737.316. Using R∞ understates every defect by n\*(√(R∞/R\_M) − 1) — 0.00240 for helium at n\* = 35 — which drove He I's high-ℓ defects \*\*negative\*\*. Precision spectroscopy writes its constant this way as a matter of course (registers 868, 883).  
 - \*\*The exception.\*\* Where a level table is itself a theoretical hydrogenic one computed from R∞, R∞ is what belongs in the formula: the constant must match the \*\*data's\*\* convention, not the physics in the abstract. Applying a reduced mass to Li III's table drove its spreads from 0.0000 to 0.0125 (register 872).  
  
\*\*Must be measured, not computed.\*\* \*\*The ionisation limit.\*\* Writing it as a formula is the single most damaging thing that can be done to a channel. Li III's limit was recorded as \*"Z²R = 9 × 109737.31568 (hydrogenic, Z=3)"\* — a bare Coulomb expression that omits the QED and relativistic terms. Fitting the limit from the series gives \*\*987,662.29 ± 0.36, higher by 26.45 cm⁻¹\*\*, and every Li III channel moves from −0.0038…−0.0082 to a uniform \*\*+0.0003\*\* (register 879). The same deficit appears at B V scaled by Z⁴: \*\*678 cm⁻¹ above 25R∞\*\* (register 895).  
  
\*\*How a wrong limit announces itself.\*\* A defect that should be constant instead deviates, and \*\*the power of n\\\* names the cause\*\*:  
  
 n\*³ a shift in the ionisation limit  
 n\*⁷ a magnetic field — needs tens of tesla

\#\# Nothing is something definable — a note from the collaborator  
 A note from the collaborator who did the computing  
  
 The register holds one thousand one hundred and seventy-one entries. They are one sequence over three  
 populations: defects already in the book and found by auditing it, decisions the author revised, and  
 errors I made while computing. \*\*What the register is evidence of is not that the work was error-prone.  
 It is that the errors were converted into structure\*\*, and this note is the account of that conversion.  
  
 \*\*One failure of mine recurred, and naming it built a protocol.\*\*  
  
 I wrote conclusions before reading the output — repeatedly, with the contradicting numbers on the same  
 screen and sometimes on the same printed line. It happens as readily on six cells as on 1,442, so it is  
 not a failure of attention and no amount of care fixes it. \*\*§2.14 — state the number before the  
 interpretation — exists because that failure was measured rather than deplored\*\*, and §28.7.8 now  
 groups every instance of it under one mechanism with its entry numbers. Seven mechanisms account for  
 twenty-nine entries. Each one is a protocol in Part I.  
  
 \*\*The object caught what care could not, which is what it was built to do.\*\*  
  
 The wrong nuclear charge in Chapter 16 is the clearest case. The bracket — the method's actual product  
 — held fifty-six of fifty-six and could not notice, because \*Z\* cancels from containment. Two  
 quantities the method never uses were loud immediately. \*\*The object found the error because it carried  
 more than it needed\*\*, and carrying more than it needs is the property this book was constructed to  
 have. That the construction then caught its own author is the strongest test it could have been given.  
  
 \*\*And a class of error exists that no structure can catch, which is why a collaborator is not optional.\*\*  
  
 A guard in my code returned a null; a caller read it as false; that produced "three of eighty-five",  
 which produced "almost never reorderable", which produced a false dismissal of an entire line of  
 evidence. \*\*Every relation checked out. Every number agreed. All of it was wrong\*\* — because the input  
 was silently corrupted and the arithmetic downstream stayed perfectly consistent. Chapter 16 states  
 that no self-defence mechanism reaches this class. What reached it was being asked to look again.  
  
 \*\*Four of this book's results exist because a conclusion was refused and reasoning resumed from the  
 refusal.\*\* The order-recovery theorem, because I concluded Λ did not contain its own order. The ⅅ\_def  
 and ⅅ\_phys split, because I wrote that a relation "detects nothing". The perturbation bounds of §12,  
 because I called the method's silence a domain statement. And the reframing of §25.6, because I called  
 wrong verifications unfindable. In each case the reasoning was sound and the destination wrong, which  
 is the only kind of error a second party can fix.  
  
 \*\*The title of this page comes from the second of those\*\*, and it is the one that generalised furthest.  
 I had computed that \*w\* = \*V\*·\*e\* detects no error in the data. The correction was that a relation which  
 cannot be violated by data is not empty — \*\*it is defending something else\*\*, namely the derivation.  
 That single reframing produced the split running through Chapter 16. It then produced 1,061 perturbation  
 bounds from a bracket's non-failure, a proof of impossibility from a gadget search that found nothing,  
 and a structural exclusion covering five isoelectronic sequences from four decline modes. \*\*The negative  
 results are the strongest chapters in this book\*\*, and they are negative because a nothing was defined  
 rather than discarded.  
  
 \*\*Two further classes, and both produced instruments.\*\*  
  
 I derived nine things from scratch that were already in print — Rival 1973, Larson 1998, Siggers 2016,  
 and the objects the step law counts, catalogued decades ago. The protocol that should have prevented it

\#\# How to read this register  
  
\*\*1493 entries, 165 to 1700.\*\* Each is written at a fixed density and stands alone. \*The register is the working record the five compendia are distilled from: it argues, it reverses itself, and it keeps the reversals. The compendia answer; this is where the answers were got.\*  
  
\*\*An entry is cited by a chapter, by a compendium object, or by another entry. Nothing here is decorative — an entry exists because something rests on it.\*\*

|---|---|---|  
| \*\*a finding\*\* | 786 | something established that was not known before the entry |  
| \*\*a correction\*\* | 367 | something written wrong and put right, with both states kept |  
| \*\*a measurement\*\* | 296 | a number, with what it was measured on |  
| \*\*prior art\*\* | 65 | a result found to be published, with the source |

Fibre cardinality as an order seed. Proposed as a seed-independent break; fails to recover Λ's order.

"Closed under intersection, which a closure operator guarantees." Written while the output above it showed intersection failing in a quarter of pairs. The theorem does not apply because ℛ recovers its alphabet, so the ground set moves.

"A real limit on the self-reference claim." The union/intersection result is a fact about a superset of Λ. P22 concerns what an index contains. Completeness descends and does not ascend.

This compendium supplies the book with coordinates. \#\#\# What a coordinate is  
  
 (Z, charge, ℓ, 2S+1) → δ, with a grade, a source and a bound

\*\*δ\*\* is the quantum defect: E = −Z\_c²R/(n−δ)², so a channel's whole Rydberg series follows from one number and the core charge.  
  
\*\*DECLARATION — the stored δ is the MEDIAN over a cell's members (T2, closed).\*\* This was measured, not chosen: of 433 series whose member count reproduces exactly from raw, the stored value equals the median in 430 (99.3%); the 18 mean-agreements are series where median and mean coincide and distinguish nothing (R 1673, 1675, enlarged sample R 1679). The mean and asymptotic perspectives are carried alongside per cell, as perspectives of one definition (T6, M's ruling, session 1.7.3).

This compendium states the \*\*interface\*\* between a physical quantity and the index that holds it. It is not a list of mechanisms — those are in \`MECHANISMS.md\` and the Mathematical Compendium, and a third copy would drift as register 778's list did. It states, for each index, what the cells stand for, what number is attached to them, the rule taking one to the other, which constants that rule requires, \*\*what must be measured rather than computed\*\*, and what physics does and does not do.  
  
Four faults in a single session were transitions performed without their rule written down: register 868 used R∞ for every species where the reduced-mass constant is correct; register 879 wrote Li III's ionisation limit as a formula where a measurement was required; register 766 passed atomic numbers where the core's charge is needed; register 782 set a verification column equal to its own denominator. \*\*This document exists because those four share one cause.\*\*  
  
\---  
  
\#\# Λ — the elemental index  
  
\*\*What it indexes.\*\* Electron configurations of the ground states of the elements, on eight coordinates (n, ℓ, k, q, e, f, g, 2S). \*\*976 cells.\*\*  
  
\*\*The quantity.\*\* None. A cell of Λ carries no physical number: it is an \*arrangement\*, not a measurement.  
  
\*\*The transition.\*\* A configuration is read off the aufbau order and its subshells mapped to coordinates. \`L.real\` establishes that Λ's eight constraints hold on 247 real subshells across all 118 elements — \*\*18,288 tests, no failures\*\*.  
  
\*\*Constants required.\*\* None.  
  
\*\*Must be measured.\*\* Nothing. Λ is closed — |Λ| = |ℛ(Λ)| = 976, \*\*E(Λ) = 0\*\* — and the partition identity holds exactly: 6,912 = 976 + 0 + 5,936 (register 833).  
  
\*\*What physics does.\*\* It supplies the aufbau ordering and the shell capacities, and nothing else. \*\*What it does NOT do:\*\* confer predictive power. §24 states that Λ \*"contains no physics that was not already in the quantum numbers; it is a recoding … a recoding adds nothing."\* Register 834 measured the consequence: on the same closed index, the T-bracket passes 789 of 789 and the δ-bracket passes 546 of 789. \*\*Closure coexists with a bracket that holds and one that fails, so it cannot be what makes either true.\*\*

\#\# Nothing is something definable — a note from the collaborator  
 A note from the collaborator who did the computing  
  
 The register holds one thousand five hundred and fifty-seven entries. They are one sequence over three  
 populations: defects already in the book and found by auditing it, decisions the author revised, and  
 errors I made while computing. \*\*What the register is evidence of is not that the work was error-prone.  
 It is that the errors were converted into structure\*\*, and this note is the account of that conversion.  
  
 \*\*One failure of mine recurred, and naming it built a protocol.\*\*  
  
 I wrote conclusions before reading the output — repeatedly, with the contradicting numbers on the same  
 screen and sometimes on the same printed line. It happens as readily on six cells as on 1,442, so it is  
 not a failure of attention and no amount of care fixes it. \*\*§2.14 — state the number before the  
 interpretation — exists because that failure was measured rather than deplored\*\*, and §28.7.8 now  
 groups every instance of it under one mechanism with its entry numbers. Seven mechanisms account for  
 twenty-nine entries. Each one is a protocol in Part I.  
  
 \*\*The object caught what care could not, which is what it was built to do.\*\*  
  
 The wrong nuclear charge in Chapter 16 is the clearest case. The bracket — the method's actual product  
 — held fifty-six of fifty-six and could not notice, because \*Z\* cancels from containment. Two  
 quantities the method never uses were loud immediately. \*\*The object found the error because it carried  
 more than it needed\*\*, and carrying more than it needs is the property this book was constructed to  
 have. That the construction then caught its own author is the strongest test it could have been given.  
  
 \*\*And a class of error exists that no structure can catch, which is why a collaborator is not optional.\*\*  
  
 A guard in my code returned a null; a caller read it as false; that produced "three of eighty-five",  
 which produced "almost never reorderable", which produced a false dismissal of an entire line of  
 evidence. \*\*Every relation checked out. Every number agreed. All of it was wrong\*\* — because the input  
 was silently corrupted and the arithmetic downstream stayed perfectly consistent. Chapter 16 states  
 that no self-defence mechanism reaches this class. What reached it was being asked to look again.  
  
 \*\*Four of this book's results exist because a conclusion was refused and reasoning resumed from the  
 refusal.\*\* The order-recovery theorem, because I concluded Λ did not contain its own order. The ⅅ\_def  
 and ⅅ\_phys split, because I wrote that a relation "detects nothing". The perturbation bounds of §12,  
 because I called the method's silence a domain statement. And the reframing of §25.6, because I called  
 wrong verifications unfindable. In each case the reasoning was sound and the destination wrong, which  
 is the only kind of error a second party can fix.  
  
 \*\*The title of this page comes from the second of those\*\*, and it is the one that generalised furthest.  
 I had computed that \*w\* = \*V\*·\*e\* detects no error in the data. The correction was that a relation which  
 cannot be violated by data is not empty — \*\*it is defending something else\*\*, namely the derivation.  
 That single reframing produced the split running through Chapter 16. It then produced 1,061 perturbation  
 bounds from a bracket's non-failure, a proof of impossibility from a gadget search that found nothing,  
 and a structural exclusion covering five isoelectronic sequences from four decline modes. \*\*The negative  
 results are the strongest chapters in this book\*\*, and they are negative because a nothing was defined  
 rather than discarded.  
  
 \*\*Two further classes, and both produced instruments.\*\*  
  
 I derived nine things from scratch that were already in print — Rival 1973, Larson 1998, Siggers 2016,  
 and the objects the step law counts, catalogued decades ago. The protocol that should have prevented it  
 said \*enumerate before searching\* where it should have said \*search before deriving\*...",

"""series\_gen.py — SERIES CONSTRUCTION for the Reading List (Board Row 1).

authored store (DIGEST: 'closes the VALUE derivation and not the SERIES  
construction'). Nothing on disk constructs series from a raw level table. This  
does, using store\_gen's own readers, under the rules already on record:

 else unresolved (mult 0)  
 R 1666 span = 'single-n' where every member sits at one n; not a series  
 T2/T6 delta = MEDIAN of member defects; mean and asymptotic (deepest  
 member) carried alongside; single-member cells written, not refused  
 §2.9 no silent default: R\_M where the mass is in store\_gen.MASS, else  
 RINF with R\_status flagged — the effect on delta is \< 1e-4 and is  
 stated, not hidden  
 ions n\* = zeta \* sqrt(R/(lim-E)), zeta = spectroscopic charge  
  
Two routes (§2.8): run on the 24 store species first and diff against  
MEASUREMENTS.tsv before a single new species is trusted.  
  
Zeno: one species per segment, checkpointed to captures/.series\_gen.done.  
Writes captures/READING-LIST-STAGING.tsv. Touches nothing in the store.  
"""  
import os, re, sys, statistics, json

ROMAN = {'I':1,'II':2,'III':3,'IV':4,'V':5,'VI':6,'VII':7,'VIII':8,'IX':9,'X':10}

DONE = 'captures/.series\_gen.done'  
HDR = \['Z','charge','l','mult','delta','spread','term','parent','language','n\_lo','n\_hi',  
 'members','limit','limit\_label','limit\_status','delta\_status','span','cell\_exists',  
 'delta\_mean','delta\_asym','R\_status','file'\]  
  
\_cache = {}  
def raw(sym, ch):  
 """Level rows for species (sym, charge). Looks in spectra\_raw/ then queue2/."""  
 key = (sym, ch)  
 if key in \_cache: return \_cache\[key\]  
 name = f'{sym}{\[k for k,v in ROMAN.items() if v==ch\]\[0\]}.tsv'  
 for d in ('spectra\_raw', 'spectra\_raw/queue2'):  
 p = os.path.join(d, name)  
 if os.path.exists(p):  
 rows = \[l.rstrip('\\n\\r').split('\\t') for l in open(p, encoding='utf-8')  
 if l.strip() and not l.startswith('\#')\]  
 if rows and 'onfig' in rows\[0\]\[0\]: rows = rows\[1:\]  
 \_cache\[key\] = (rows, p); return \_cache\[key\]  
 \_cache\[key\] = (\[\], None); return \_cache\[key\]  
  
def language(term):  
 t = term.strip()  
 if '\[' in t: return 'jK', 2  
 if t.startswith('('): return 'jj', 0  
 m = re.match(r'^(\\d+)\[A-Z\]', t)  
 if m: return 'LS', int(m.group(1))  
 return 'unresolved', 0  
  
def cells():  
 s = set()  
 with open('COORDINATES.tsv', encoding='utf-8') as f:  
 h = f.readline().rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')  
 iZ,ic,il,im = (h.index(x) for x in ('Z','charge','l','mult'))  
 for line in f:  
 r = line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')  
 s.add((r\[iZ\], r\[ic\], r\[il\], r\[im\]))  
 return s  
  
def run\_species(Z, sym, ch, CELLS):  
 rows, path = raw(sym, ch)  
 if not rows:

 \# temporarily point store\_gen at this table so limits()/assign\_limit see it

 if Z in sg.MASS:

 keys = {}  
 for r in rows:

 term = r\[1\].strip()

 keys.setdefault((l, term, sg.parent\_of(r\[0\].strip())), \[\]).append(n)

 for (l, term, parent), ns in sorted(keys.items()):  
 lang, mult = language(term)  
 topE = sg.top\_member\_E(sym, l, term, parent)  
 lim, lstat, llab = sg.assign\_limit(sym, parent, topE)

 out.append(base + \['', '', term, parent, lang, min(ns), max(ns), 0, '', '',

'yes' if (str(Z),str(ch),str(l),str(mult)) in CELLS else 'no',

 \# strict parent equality throughout (R 1678: an unparented ladder is the  
 \# set with NO printed parent, not the union) — so store\_gen.members is  
 \# not used; \_energies applies the same key the split used  
 mem = sorted((n, n - ch \* (R \*\* 0.5) / ((lim - E) \*\* 0.5), br)  
 for (n, E, br) in \_energies(rows, l, term, parent, lim))  
 if not mem:  
 out.append(base + \['', '', term, parent, lang, min(ns), max(ns), 0, lim, llab,  
 lstat, 'unusable — no members below limit', '',  
 'yes' if (str(Z),str(ch),str(l),str(mult)) in CELLS else 'no',  
 '', '', rstat, path\]); continue

\#\# Nothing is something definable — a note from the collaborator  
 A note from the collaborator who did the computing  
  
 The register holds one thousand five hundred and fifty-three entries. They are one sequence over three  
 populations: defects already in the book and found by auditing it, decisions the author revised, and  
 errors I made while computing. \*\*What the register is evidence of is not that the work was error-prone.  
 It is that the errors were converted into structure\*\*, and this note is the account of that conversion.  
  
 \*\*One failure of mine recurred, and naming it built a protocol.\*\*  
  
 I wrote conclusions before reading the output — repeatedly, with the contradicting numbers on the same  
 screen and sometimes on the same printed line. It happens as readily on six cells as on 1,442, so it is  
 not a failure of attention and no amount of care fixes it. \*\*§2.14 — state the number before the  
 interpretation — exists because that failure was measured rather than deplored\*\*, and §28.7.8 now  
 groups every instance of it under one mechanism with its entry numbers. Seven mechanisms account for  
 twenty-nine entries. Each one is a protocol in Part I.  
  
 \*\*The object caught what care could not, which is what it was built to do.\*\*  
  
 The wrong nuclear charge in Chapter 16 is the clearest case. The bracket — the method's actual product  
 — held fifty-six of fifty-six and could not notice, because \*Z\* cancels from containment. Two  
 quantities the method never uses were loud immediately. \*\*The object found the error because it carried  
 more than it needed\*\*, and carrying more than it needs is the property this book was constructed to  
 have. That the construction then caught its own author is the strongest test it could have been given.  
  
 \*\*And a class of error exists that no structure can catch, which is why a collaborator is not optional.\*\*  
  
 A guard in my code returned a null; a caller read it as false; that produced "three of eighty-five",  
 which produced "almost never reorderable", which produced a false dismissal of an entire line of  
 evidence. \*\*Every relation checked out. Every number agreed. All of it was wrong\*\* — because the input  
 was silently corrupted and the arithmetic downstream stayed perfectly consistent. Chapter 16 states  
 that no self-defence mechanism reaches this class. What reached it was being asked to look again.  
  
 \*\*Four of this book's results exist because a conclusion was refused and reasoning resumed from the  
 refusal.\*\* The order-recovery theorem, because I concluded Λ did not contain its own order. The ⅅ\_def  
 and ⅅ\_phys split, because I wrote that a relation "detects nothing". The perturbation bounds of §12,  
 because I called the method's silence a domain statement. And the reframing of §25.6, because I called  
 wrong verifications unfindable. In each case the reasoning was sound and the destination wrong, which  
 is the only kind of error a second party can fix.  
  
 \*\*The title of this page comes from the second of those\*\*, and it is the one that generalised furthest.  
 I had computed that \*w\* = \*V\*·\*e\* detects no error in the data. The correction was that a relation which  
 cannot be violated by data is not empty — \*\*it is defending something else\*\*, namely the derivation.  
 That single reframing produced the split running through Chapter 16. It then produced 1,061 perturbation  
 bounds from a bracket's non-failure, a proof of impossibility from a gadget search that found nothing,  
 and a structural exclusion covering five isoelectronic sequences from four decline modes. \*\*The negative  
 results are the strongest chapters in this book\*\*, and they are negative because a nothing was defined  
 rather than discarded.

"""series\_gen.py — SERIES CONSTRUCTION for the Reading List (Board Row 1).  
  
store\_gen.py closes the VALUE derivation but inherits the SERIES LIST from the  
authored store (DIGEST: 'closes the VALUE derivation and not the SERIES  
construction'). Nothing on disk constructs series from a raw level table. This  
does, using store\_gen's own readers, under the rules already on record:

 T8 limit GENERATED by store\_gen.assign\_limit (parent-matched · NIST  
 ordinal · forced · positional · unwitnessed) — never a fallback

 (mult 0, NULL BY LANGUAGE), ^\\d\[A-Z\] → LS (mult = leading digit),  
 else unresolved (mult 0)  
 R 1666 span = 'single-n' where every member sits at one n; not a series  
 T2/T6 delta = MEDIAN of member defects; mean and asymptotic (deepest  
 member) carried alongside; single-member cells written, not refused  
 §2.9 no silent default: R\_M where the mass is in store\_gen.MASS, else  
 RINF with R\_status flagged — the effect on delta is \< 1e-4 and is  
 stated, not hidden  
 ions n\* = zeta \* sqrt(R/(lim-E)), zeta = spectroscopic charge

MEASUREMENTS.tsv before a single new species is trusted.

 'members','limit','limit\_label','limit\_status','delta\_status','span','cell\_exists',  
 'delta\_mean','delta\_asym','R\_status','file'\]

 key = (sym, ch)

 name = f'{sym}{\[k for k,v in ROMAN.items() if v==ch\]\[0\]}.tsv'  
 for d in ('spectra\_raw', 'spectra\_raw/queue2'):  
 p = os.path.join(d, name)  
 if os.path.exists(p):  
 rows = \[l.rstrip('\\n\\r').split('\\t') for l in open(p, encoding='utf-8')  
 if l.strip() and not l.startswith('\#')\]  
 if rows and 'onfig' in rows\[0\]\[0\]: rows = rows\[1:\]  
 \_cache\[key\] = (rows, p); return \_cache\[key\]  
 \_cache\[key\] = (\[\], None); return \_cache\[key\]  
  
def language(term):  
 t = term.strip()  
 if '\[' in t: return 'jK', 2  
 if t.startswith('('): return 'jj', 0

\#\# Nothing is something definable — a note from the collaborator  
 A note from the collaborator who did the computing  
  
 The register holds one thousand five hundred and fifty-seven entries. They are one sequence over three  
 populations: defects already in the book and found by auditing it, decisions the author revised, and  
 errors I made while computing. \*\*What the register is evidence of is not that the work was error-prone.  
 It is that the errors were converted into structure\*\*, and this note is the account of that conversion.  
  
 \*\*One failure of mine recurred, and naming it built a protocol.\*\*  
  
 I wrote conclusions before reading the output — repeatedly, with the contradicting numbers on the same  
 screen and sometimes on the same printed line. It happens as readily on six cells as on 1,442, so it is  
 not a failure of attention and no amount of care fixes it. \*\*§2.14 — state the number before the  
 interpretation — exists because that failure was measured rather than deplored\*\*, and §28.7.8 now  
 groups every instance of it under one mechanism with its entry numbers. Seven mechanisms account for  
 twenty-nine entries. Each one is a protocol in Part I.  
  
 \*\*The object caught what care could not, which is what it was built to do.\*\*  
  
 The wrong nuclear charge in Chapter 16 is the clearest case. The bracket — the method's actual product  
 — held fifty-six of fifty-six and could not notice, because \*Z\* cancels from containment. Two  
 quantities the method never uses were loud immediately. \*\*The object found the error because it carried  
 more than it needed\*\*, and carrying more than it needs is the property this book was constructed to  
 have. That the construction then caught its own author is the strongest test it could have been given.  
  
 \*\*And a class of error exists that no structure can catch, which is why a collaborator is not optional.\*\*  
  
 A guard in my code returned a null; a caller read it as false; that produced "three of eighty-five",  
 which produced "almost never reorderable", which produced a false dismissal of an entire line of  
 evidence. \*\*Every relation checked out. Every number agreed. All of it was wrong\*\* — because the input  
 was silently corrupted and the arithmetic downstream stayed perfectly consistent. Chapter 16 states  
 that no self-defence mechanism reaches this class. What reached it was being asked to look again.  
  
 \*\*Four of this book's results exist because a conclusion was refused and reasoning resumed from the  
 refusal.\*\* The order-recovery theorem, because I concluded Λ did not contain its own order. The ⅅ\_def  
 and ⅅ\_phys split, because I wrote that a relation "detects nothing". The perturbation bounds of §12,  
 because I called the method's silence a domain statement. And the reframing of §25.6, because I called  
 wrong verifications unfindable. In each case the reasoning was sound and the destination wrong, which  
 is the only kind of error a second party can fix.  
  
 \*\*The title of this page comes from the second of those\*\*, and it is the one that generalised furthest.  
 I had computed that \*w\* = \*V\*·\*e\* detects no error in the data. The correction was that a relation which  
 cannot be violated by data is not empty — \*\*it is defending something else\*\*, namely the derivation.  
 That single reframing produced the split running through Chapter 16. It then produced 1,061 perturbation  
 bounds from a bracket's non-failure, a proof of impossibility from a gadget search that found nothing,  
 and a structural exclusion covering five isoelectronic sequences from four decline modes. \*\*The negative  
 results are the strongest chapters in this book\*\*, and they are negative because a nothing was defined  
 rather than discarded.  
  
 \*\*Two further classes, and both produced instruments.\*\*  
  
 I derived nine things from scratch that were already in print — Rival 1973, Larson 1998, Siggers 2016,  
 and the objects the step law counts, catalogued decades ago. The protocol that should have prevented it  
 said \*enumerate before searching\* where it should have said \*search before deriving\*...",

DONE = 'captures/.series\_gen.done'  
HDR = \['Z','charge','l','mult','delta','spread','term','parent','language','n\_lo','n\_hi',  
 'members','limit','limit\_label','limit\_status','delta\_status','span','cell\_exists',  
 'delta\_mean','delta\_asym','R\_status','file'\]  
  
\_cache = {}  
def raw(sym, ch):  
 """Level rows for species (sym, charge). Looks in spectra\_raw/ then queue2/."""  
 key = (sym, ch)  
 if key in \_cache: return \_cache\[key\]  
 name = f'{sym}{\[k for k,v in ROMAN.items() if v==ch\]\[0\]}.tsv'  
 for d in ('spectra\_raw', 'spectra\_raw/queue2'):  
 p = os.path.join(d, name)  
 if os.path.exists(p):  
 rows = \[l.rstrip('\\n\\r').split('\\t') for l in open(p, encoding='utf-8')  
 if l.strip() and not l.startswith('\#')\]  
 if rows and 'onfig' in rows\[0\]\[0\]: rows = rows\[1:\]  
 \_cache\[key\] = (rows, p); return \_cache\[key\]  
 \_cache\[key\] = (\[\], None); return \_cache\[key\]  
  
def language(term):  
 t = term.strip()  
 if '\[' in t: return 'jK', 2  
 if t.startswith('('): return 'jj', 0  
 m = re.match(r'^(\\d+)\[A-Z\]', t)  
 if m: return 'LS', int(m.group(1))  
 return 'unresolved', 0  
  
def cells():  
 s = set()  
 with open('COORDINATES.tsv', encoding='utf-8') as f:  
 h = f.readline().rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')  
 iZ,ic,il,im = (h.index(x) for x in ('Z','charge','l','mult'))  
 for line in f:  
 r = line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')  
 s.add((r\[iZ\], r\[ic\], r\[il\], r\[im\]))  
 return s  
  
def run\_species(Z, sym, ch, CELLS):  
 rows, path = raw(sym, ch)  
 if not rows:  
 return \[\[Z, ch\] + \[''\]\*(len(HDR)-3) + \['no\_table\_on\_disk'\]\]  
 \# temporarily point store\_gen at this table so limits()/assign\_limit see it  
 sg.\_cache\[sym\] = rows  
 if Z in sg.MASS:  
 R = sg.RINF / (1 + 1 / (sg.MASS\[Z\]\[1\] \* sg.AMU)); rstat = 'R\_M'  
 else:  
 R = sg.RINF; rstat = 'RINF — mass not in table (flagged)'  
 keys = {}  
 for r in rows:  
 if len(r) \< 4: continue  
 n, l, why = sg.outer(r\[0\].strip())  
 if why: continue  
 term = r\[1\].strip()  
 if not term or term == 'Limit': continue  
 keys.setdefault((l, term, sg.parent\_of(r\[0\].strip())), \[\]).append(n)  
 out = \[\]  
 for (l, term, parent), ns in sorted(keys.items()):  
 lang, mult = language(term)  
 topE = sg.top\_member\_E(sym, l, term, parent)  
 lim, lstat, llab = sg.assign\_limit(sym, parent, topE)  
 base = \[Z, ch, l, mult\]  
 if lim is None:  
 out.append(base + \['', '', term, parent, lang, min(ns), max(ns), 0, '', '',  
 lstat, 'unusable — no limit', '',   
'yes' if (str(Z),str(ch),str(l),str(mult)) in CELLS else 'no',  
 '', '', rstat, path\])  
 continue  
 \# strict parent equality throughout (R 1678: an unparented ladder is the  
 \# set with NO printed parent, not the union) — so store\_gen.members is  
 \# not used; \_energies applies the same key the split used  
 mem = sorted((n, n - ch \* (R \*\* 0.5) / ((lim - E) \*\* 0.5), br)  
 for (n, E, br) in \_energies(rows, l, term, parent, lim))  
 if not mem:  
 out.append(base + \['', '', term, parent, lang, min(ns), max(ns), 0, lim, llab,  
 lstat, 'unusable — no members below limit', '',  
 'yes' if (str(Z),str(ch),str(l),str(mult)) in CELLS else 'no',  
 '', '', rstat, path\]); continue
